title: Duality Identity: M_r(z) = M_{-r}(z⁻¹)⁻¹
content: power_mean_neg_inv establishes the algebraic identity that converts negative-exponent power means to positive-exponent ones on inverted values. The proof has two parts: (1) showing the sums are equal, ∑ wᵢ(zᵢ⁻¹)^(-r) = ∑ wᵢzᵢ^r, by rewriting each term via Real.inv_rpow + Real.rpow_neg + inv_inv; (2) showing the powers match, A^(1/r) = (A^(1/(-r)))⁻¹, since 1/(-r) = -(1/r) and Real.rpow_neg gives A^(-(1/r)) = (A^(1/r))⁻¹. The identity is the key enabler for the negative monotonicity proof.

title: Positivity: Weighted Sum and Power Mean Are Positive
content: Two helper lemmas establish positivity. weighted_sum_pos: since ∑ wᵢ = 1 > 0 and all wᵢ ≥ 0, there exists some i₀ with wᵢ₀ > 0 (by contradiction — if all wᵢ = 0, the sum would be 0 ≠ 1). Then wᵢ₀ · zᵢ₀^p > 0 is a positive term in the sum, so ∑ wᵢzᵢ^p ≥ wᵢ₀ · zᵢ₀^p > 0 by Finset.single_le_sum. weightedPowerMean_pos follows immediately via Real.rpow_pos_of_pos.
mathContext: If $\sum_i w_i = 1$ with $w_i \geq 0$ and $z_i > 0$, then $\sum_i w_i z_i^p > 0$ and $M_p = (\sum_i w_i z_i^p)^{1/p} > 0$.

title: Main Theorem: M_r ≤ M_s for r ≤ s < 0
content: power_mean_monotone_neg is the main result. The proof proceeds in three stages: (1) Negate exponents: since r ≤ t < 0, we have 0 < -t ≤ -r. (2) Apply power_mean_monotone_pos to z⁻¹ with exponents -t and -r: M_{-t}(z⁻¹) ≤ M_{-r}(z⁻¹). (3) Invert: using the duality identity, M_r(z) = M_{-r}(z⁻¹)⁻¹ and M_t(z) = M_{-t}(z⁻¹)⁻¹. Since A = M_{-t}(z⁻¹) ≤ B = M_{-r}(z⁻¹) and 0 < A, we need B⁻¹ ≤ A⁻¹. This is proved via explicit calc: 1 = A·A⁻¹ ≤ B·A⁻¹ (by mul_le_mul_of_nonneg_right), then multiply by B⁻¹ and simplify with mul_assoc + mul_inv_cancel₀ + mul_one.
mathContext: Given $r \leq t < 0$: let $z' = z^{-1}$. Then $0 < -t \leq -r$ so $M_{-t}(z') \leq M_{-r}(z')$. By duality: $M_r(z) = M_{-r}(z')^{-1} \leq M_{-t}(z')^{-1} = M_t(z)$. The inversion uses: $1 = A \cdot A^{-1} \leq B \cdot A^{-1}$, so $B^{-1} \leq B^{-1} \cdot B \cdot A^{-1} = A^{-1}$.

title: Harmonic Mean ≤ Geometric Mean as Power Mean Corollary
content: The classical inequality HM ≤ GM is the $r = -1$ case of the power mean chain. Here it is proved via `harmonic_mean_le_geom_mean_direct` (a standalone proof from the parent file), with the `_hHM` hypothesis documenting the connection: $M_{-1}(z,w) = (\sum w_i / z_i)^{-1}$ is exactly the weighted harmonic mean. This theorem demonstrates how classical named inequalities (HM-GM, AM-GM, QM-AM) are all specializations of a single monotonicity result.

title: The Power Mean Interpolation Chain: Status Summary
content: A documentation theorem summarizing the full power mean chain $\min(z) \leq \cdots \leq \text{HM} \leq \text{GM} \leq \text{AM} \leq M_2 \leq \cdots \leq \max(z)$, marking which links are proved. Seven results are marked [✓]: GM ≤ AM (from Mathlib), AM ≤ M_p for p ≥ 1 (Mathlib), GM ≤ M_p for p ≥ 1, Jensen's inequality, HM ≤ GM (proved here), positive monotonicity (proved here), and negative monotonicity (proved here via duality). Only the mixed-sign crossing (r < 0 < s, requiring the r → 0 limit) remains as an axiom.
mathContext: $\min(z) \leq \cdots \leq M_{-1} = \text{HM} \leq M_0 = \text{GM} \leq M_1 = \text{AM} \leq M_2 \leq \cdots \leq \max(z)$. Proved: $M_r \leq M_s$ for $0 < r \leq s$ and for $r \leq s < 0$. Remaining: $r < 0 < s$ (mixed sign).
